parts:
The frustrating thing is, sometimes it seems to really fuck things up and I can’t get anything to run.  See Rstudio script below.  


> setwd("~/AndrewFiles/research/loo_stan")
> source("stan.R")
> source("loo.R")
> source("vgis_new.R")
> 
> wells <- read.csv("wells.csv")
> N <- nrow(wells)
> X <- cbind(rep(1,N), wells$dist100, wells$arsenic)
> y <- wells$y
> 
> K <- ncol(X)
> 
> fit <- stan("logistic.stan", data=nlist(N, K, X, y), iter=2000, chains=4)
Loading required package: parallel
Error in rstan::sflist2stanfit(out) :
The following elements of 'sflist' do not contain samples: 1, 2, 3, 4.

  could not find function "cpp_object_initializer"
failed to create the sampler; sampling not done
> 
> # Now I will remove logistic.rda from the directory
> # OK, I just removed it.  I'll try again.
> fit <- stan("logistic.stan", data=nlist(N, K, X, y), iter=2000, chains=4)

Then I closed R, deleted the .rda file, reopened R, and I still couldn’t get it to run:

TRANSLATING MODEL 'logistic' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
COMPILING THE C++ CODE FOR MODEL 'logistic' NOW.
Error in .Object$initialize(...) : 
  could not find function "cpp_object_initializer"
Error in .Object$initialize(...) : 
  could not find function "cpp_object_initializer"
failed to create the sampler; sampling not done


So then I’m like, fuck it, I’ll close and reopen R and just run it using basic stan(), not the version in stan.R.  This works just fine.  But it takes 4 times as long to run, which kinda sucks.

_Then_, I source(“stan.R”) and run it, and it’s fine.  So, for some reason, it seems to require running basic stan() to clear out some cobwebs before I can go back to using stan.R.

Pretty annoying, huh?

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: running stan.R
parts: It doesn't put the rstan package on the search path. That way someone can add the stan() function in stan.R to their .Rprofile and it won't load the rstan package if they don't use it.
